If we assume Conjecture 1, we obtain a similar result to Corollary 17 using Theorem 15.
When n = 8 we get (2n − 1)/3 = 85 so the 85-th roots of unity will appear.

7 Final Remarks

Returning to Remark 5 at the end of Section 3, Conjecture 1 states that (12) implies
αq+2 = 1, when d = 2 and n is even. We are unable to prove this conjecture, but somehow
it is important to this problem. A full investigation of the implications of Conjecture 1,
as well as its proof, is a topic for future work. Also, generalizations of Conjecture 1 for
d > 2 are probably available.

The motivation for Conjecture 1 is that if αq+2 = 1, then the equation in the statement of
Theorem 3 is automatically satisfied. Furthermore, equation (6) which says

− α−1 has norm 1 this equation always has q − 1 solutions for x by Hilbert Theorem 90.
